title: The New Nixon Shock? Why Japan Fears a Trump-Xi Deal
author: Jio Kamata
text:
Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi Sanae meets with U.S. President Donald Trump on the sidelines of the U.N. General Assembly in New York, Sep. 22, 2026, one day before Chinese President Xi Jinping arrived for a state visit to the United States.
Credit: X/ Takaichi Sanae
The latest China-U.S. summit, held from September 23 to 25, raised concerns in Japan, not so much because of its substance as because of how it appeared. Japanese media have paid particular attention to Donald Trump and Xi Jinping’s references to their respective countries as former “allies” that fought against imperial Japan, as well as to Trump’s apparent intentions. Within the Japanese government, “confusion” has reportedly been expressed internally.Before the summit, the Japanese government had been preparing for the worst-case scenario, a concern presumably heightened by the U.S. president’s suggestion, immediately after his previous summit with Xi, that arms shipments to Taiwan could be used as a possible “negotiation tool.” [...]
